messages.text: Can I get TennCare? I'm a dad with two kids and I lost my work insurance.

I can help you check. I need a few facts first.

1. How old are you and your two kids?
2. What is your household's income before taxes? Please tell me how much each person earns and how often they're paid (weekly, every two weeks, or monthly). Include any other income, like unemployment or child support you receive.

I'm 39. My kids are 2 and 9. It's just the three of us.

I make $2,350 a month before taxes. I get paid monthly, and that's the only income. No child support, no unemployment, nothing else coming in.

**Your kids will likely qualify for TennCare, and you possibly will.** Here is how it looks for each of you.

- **Your 2-year-old: likely.** Your income is $2,350 a month before taxes. The limit for a child ages 1 to 5 in a household of 3 is $3,233 a month (142% of the poverty level).
- **Your 9-year-old: likely.** The limit for a child ages 6 to 18 in a household of 3 is $3,028 a month (133% of the poverty level).
- **You: possibly.** The limit for a parent is $2,277 a month (100% of the poverty level). Your income is a little over that. But TennCare takes off an extra 5% of the poverty level when it counts income, so you could still fit. A caseworker will make that call.

Sources: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide, Division of TennCare](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html) and [42 CFR 435.603, the 5% income rule](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/section-435.603).

**How to apply for TennCare and CoverKids**
- Go to [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/), or call 855-259-0701.
- Losing your work insurance doesn't stop you from applying. Anyone can apply, and only the state agency decides.

**Two other programs that look likely**
- **Food assistance (SNAP): likely, about $309 a month.** This is only an estimate. I didn't ask about savings. The federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. I also didn't use your rent or bills, and those could raise the amount. Apply through [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287. Source: [USDA's 2026-27 SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola).
- **WIC: likely, for your 2-year-old.** Your income is under the $4,212 a month limit for 3 people. WIC also does a short health and nutrition check at the clinic. Apply at a local health department clinic or call 1-800-342-5942. Sources: [USDA WIC income limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926) and [Tennessee Department of Health](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).

For free local help applying, you can dial 211.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the agency decides who qualifies. Be sure to report your income and household accurately on the applications.

If you'd like a closer SNAP estimate, tell me your rent or mortgage, whether you pay heating or cooling separately, and any child care costs.
rent is $900. i pay heating/cooling on top of that, around $80-120 depending on the season. daycare for my 2 year old is $300 a month. thanks for looking into this

Thanks. With your rent, heating and cooling, and daycare included, **your food assistance (SNAP) estimate goes up to about $610 a month**. That's still only an estimate, and the result is still "likely." Your TennCare and WIC results haven't changed.

**How the SNAP estimate works**
- Your income is $2,350 a month before taxes.
- SNAP takes off 20% of your wages ($470) and a standard deduction ($217).
- It takes off your daycare cost ($300).
- It takes off part of your housing and utility costs ($703.50). This counts your rent plus a standard utility amount for people who pay heating or cooling.
- That leaves about $659.50 in countable income. The limit for 3 people is $2,277 a month.

Sources: [USDA's 2026-27 SNAP limits and deductions](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola) and [USDA SNAP eligibility rules](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility).

**Two things to know**
- **The utility figure may be out of date.** I used Tennessee's most recent published standard utility amount. It was in effect through 2026-09-30, and newer numbers weren't available. The caseworker will use the current one, so your amount could change a little. Source: [USDA's standard utility allowances](https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/2026-05-21-SUA-Table-FY26.xlsx).
- **Savings.** The federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. I haven't asked about your savings. If you're over that, let me know or ask the caseworker.

**Next steps**
- **TennCare and CoverKids:** your kids are likely, and you are possibly. Apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- **SNAP:** apply through [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287.
- **WIC:** likely for your 2-year-old. Apply at a local health department clinic or call 1-800-342-5942. WIC also does a short health and nutrition check.
- **Free local help:** dial 211.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides who qualifies, and you can apply either way. Please report your income, rent and daycare costs accurately on the applications. If you get too much in benefits, you may have to pay it back.

You're welcome. I hope this helps.
Okay, thanks. Quick question: do I have to pick one thing to apply for, or can I do TennCare, SNAP, and WIC all at once? Also, do I need to bring proof of my income or the daycare bill when I apply?

**Yes, you can apply for all three. You don't have to pick one.** They are separate applications at separate places. I didn't find an official source that says one application covers all three programs.

- **TennCare:** [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or 855-259-0701.
- **SNAP:** [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or 866-311-4287.
- **WIC:** a local health department clinic or 1-800-342-5942.

**WIC may be easier after SNAP or TennCare.** Tennessee's WIC page says: "Adjunctive Eligibility allows WIC applicants to be automatically income-eligible for WIC if they show proof of participation in any of the following programs: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)... Tennessee Medicaid (TennCare)." If one of those gets approved first, bring the approval letter to WIC. You can also apply for WIC right away. (Source: [Tennessee Department of Health](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).)

**Proof of income and daycare costs**
- **SNAP:** Yes, expect to give proof. USDA says that after you apply, "you will need to complete an eligibility interview and give proof (verification) of the information you provided." The interview is usually by phone or in person. The state usually sends a decision within 30 days. (Source: [USDA SNAP Eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility).)
- **Daycare costs:** The SNAP rules let you deduct daycare costs when you need the care to work. Tennessee's policy says there's no limit on the amount. (Sources: [7 CFR 273.9](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-273.9) and [Tennessee SNAP Policy 24.18](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.18%20SNAP%20Deductions%20from%20Income_Esigned.pdf).) I didn't find a list of which papers they accept. Having a recent daycare bill or receipt handy is a good idea.
- **TennCare and WIC:** I didn't find a specific document list for either one. When you apply, ask what to bring.

**Documents worth gathering**
- Recent pay stubs.
- Your daycare bill.
- Your lease.
- Your heating or cooling bills.
- Proof of ID.

This is my suggestion, not an official list. Call each program to confirm what they need. You can also dial 211 for free help.

If a caseworker asks for something you can't get, tell them. They can often explain other ways to show it.
